title: Bound memory use while receiving SSE POST bodies
description:
## Summary

The SSE POST handler reads every request body completely into memory with `io.ReadAll` before delivering any bytes to the accepted connection. There is no configured size limit.

## Affected code

- `server.go:200-205` calls `io.ReadAll(r.Body)` and only then writes the resulting allocation into the application pipe.
- The session ID authorizes the request but imposes no resource limit.

## Impact

Any valid or compromised client can issue a single arbitrarily large POST and force a correspondingly large allocation. Multiple concurrent requests amplify the problem into process-wide memory exhaustion. Chunked requests do not need to declare their size in advance. The full buffering also adds latency and duplicates data that could be streamed.

## Proposed fix

Prefer streaming the body into a cancellation-aware inbound path rather than materializing it. Also add an explicit per-POST maximum, for example a documented `Server.MaxPostBytes` setting with a conservative default:

- Reject an oversized declared `Content-Length` immediately.
- Wrap the body with `http.MaxBytesReader` or an equivalent limiting reader for chunked requests.
- Return HTTP 413 when the limit is exceeded.
- Stop reading promptly when the request context or connection is canceled.
- Preserve stream ordering when concurrent POST requests are allowed, or explicitly serialize/reject them.
- Ensure delivery errors are returned rather than converted to HTTP 204.

The chosen default should account for expected tunnel write sizes and remain configurable for large-transfer deployments.

## Acceptance criteria

- RSS/allocation growth remains bounded when a client sends a body larger than the configured maximum.
- Oversized fixed-length and chunked bodies receive HTTP 413.
- Normal binary payloads, including bodies near the limit, are delivered exactly.
- A slow application reader and canceled client request do not leak handler goroutines.
- Concurrent POST ordering semantics are documented and tested.
- JavaScript and Go clients surface the non-204 response as a write error.
